statement.p: Joshua is paying a dinner bill of {\$20.00}. Joshua plans to pay 13\% in tips. How much in total (including bill and tip) will Joshua pay?
Joshua will pay in total (including bill and tip).

solution.p: First, we need to find how much tip Joshua paid. This problem can be boiled down to this question: What is 13\% of 20? We will show multiple methods to solve this problem.
We will use proportion to solve this problem. Assume 13\% of 20 is x, so 13 out of 100 corresponds to x out of 20.
We will write and solve the proportion:
Joshua will pay {\$2.60} in tip. In total, he will pay {\$20.00}+{\$2.60}={\$22.60}.
Joshua will pay {\$22.60} in total (including bill and tip).
We will use the percentage formula to solve this problem. This translation from English to math may help you remember the percentage formula.
The question is: What is 13\% of 20? Assume x is 13\% of 20. We have:
Joshua will pay {\$2.60} in tip. In total, he will pay {\$20.00}+{\$2.60}={\$22.60}.
Joshua will pay {\$22.60} in total (including bill and tip).

solution.p: By the formula \text{percentage} = \text{rate} \cdot \text{base}, we do a multiplication to solve the problem:
